title: AIZZAK — logs (Wave 0)
description: The searchable half of Wave 0 step 0.6. When p99 rises for two minutes the metric says THAT it happened and only the log says WHY -- `aizzak-capacity` is the first dashboard, this is the second. Provisioned from deploy/grafana/dashboards/aizzak-logs.json and not editable in the browser (step 0.5's baseline has to be reproducible from a commit). Every panel's description names the plan item it exists for.

list.name: correlation_id
list.label: correlation_id
list.description: The id from the failing response's X-Correlation-Id header or its RFC 9457 problem body. Empty means no filter.

panels.title: طلبٌ واحد، من الحافّة إلى العامل — معيار القبول لـ0.6
كلّ أسطر الطلب — $correlation_id
panels.description: THE acceptance criterion of capacity step 0.6, as one query: «استعلامٌ واحد يجمع كلّ أسطر طلبٍ فاشلٍ عبر الحافّة والتطبيق والعامل بـcorrelation_id واحد». Paste a correlation id into the variable above -- it is the `X-Correlation-Id` header on every response and the `correlation_id` field of every RFC 9457 problem body, so a user reporting a failure can hand you one. `correlation_id` is STRUCTURED METADATA, not a label: it has one value per request, and a label with that cardinality would take Loki down long before the platform (the same rule 0.2 applied to metrics). Leave the variable empty to see the whole stack unfiltered.

panels.title: أخطاء كلّ الخدمات
panels.description: Every ERROR line the stack has emitted, newest last. `level` IS a label (five bounded values), so this filter is an index lookup rather than a scan -- which is what makes it usable while a load run is in flight.

panels.title: معدّل الأسطر لكلّ خدمة
panels.description: Lines per second by service. Reading it as VOLUME is the point: a service that goes silent under load has either stopped working or stopped being collected, and both look identical on a metrics dashboard. The `alloy`/`loki` series are the pipeline reporting on itself.

panels.title: طلبات الحافّة حسب الحالة
panels.description: nginx's own access log, counted by status class. Deliberately NOT the same number as `aizzak_http_requests_total` (step 0.2): that one is what the APP served, this one is what the EDGE answered -- and the gap between them is exactly the `limit_req` rejections and the 404s the edge answers locally, which never reach the app to be counted.

panels.title: أبطأ ما مرّ بالحافّة (> 1s)
panels.description: Edge lines whose total `duration_s` exceeded one second -- the budget `07 §2` sets for a synchronous read is 150ms p95, so anything here is far outside it. Each line carries the `correlation_id` that the panel at the top of this dashboard takes.

panels.title: فشلُ المعالجات والرسائل الميتة
panels.description: The two lines an operator goes looking for when an event never produced its effect: `handler_failed` (the handler raised; the entry stays pending and is redelivered) and `dead_lettered` (attempt N=5; the entry moved to `<stream>.dlq`). Since 0.6 both carry the `correlation_id` of the REQUEST that produced the event -- so a worker traceback and the API 500 that caused it are one query apart.
